summary: The note describes closed-eye hallucinations and closed-eye visualizations (CEV), which occur with eyes closed or in a dark room and are distinct from phosphenes and other external stimuli. It lays out five levels of CEV perception, from basic visual noise (levels 1-2, very common) through patterns and motion (level 3), objects and environments (level 4), to overriding physical perception via sensory deprivation (level 5). It also distinguishes CEV from afterimages, entoptic phenomena like floaters, blue-sky sprites, and pressure phosphenes.
one_line: A classification of closed-eye hallucinations and visualizations into five levels, and how they differ from afterimages, floaters, and pressure phosphenes.
key_facts: Closed-eye hallucinations and closed-eye visualizations (CEV) occur when one's eyes are closed or when one is in a darkened room.
CEV should not be confused with phosphenes, which are perceived light and shapes produced by pressure on the retina or other non-visual stimulation of the eye.
The note identifies five known levels of CEV perception, achievable through chemical stimuli or meditative relaxation techniques.
Level 1 (visual noise) is described as a seemingly random noise of pointillistic light or dark regions with no apparent shape or order.
In a bright room, closed eyelids show a dark red color because a small amount of light penetrates the eyelids and takes on the color of the blood it has passed through.
Level 2 involves light or dark flashes, where regions of intense black, bright white, or colors such as yellow, green, or pink can appear in the noise and seem fleeting in nature.
Level 3 patterns may resemble fractals and are relatively easily accessible to people who use psychedelic drugs such as LSD.
At level 4, thoughts visually manifest as objects or environments, and the CEV noise seems to calm down and fade away, leaving an intense flat ordered blackness.
Level 5 can be entered from complete sensory deprivation, as experienced in an isolation tank or deep trance of hypnosis, but requires great relaxation.

According to lucid dreaming researcher Stephen LaBerge, an inhibitory system involving the thalamus, likely involving serotonergic neurons, keeps imaginary perceptions from becoming hallucinations, and this system is inhibited during REM sleep.
Visual burn-in from bright lights fades over a few minutes as the retina recovers, whereas waking-consciousness CEV noise does not disappear if observed continuously over a period of time.
Floaters are caused by opacities in the vitreous humour and are not CEV.
Blue-sky sprites are white blood cells moving through the blood vessels of the retina, and their motion is not uniformly random like CEV noise.
Pressure phosphenes, produced for example by lightly touching the rightmost part of the eye socket with eyes closed and looking left, are sensory distortions rather than hallucinations.
The note states that the 'visual release hallucinations' term refers to similar hallucinations that occur due to loss of vision.

entities.name: Stephen LaBerge
entities.role: lucid dreaming researcher cited for the theory that an inhibitory system involving the thalamus keeps imaginary perceptions from becoming hallucinations

entities.name: Jurij Moskvitin
entities.role: author of the quoted essay 'Essay on the origin of thought' on the difference between real and imagined worlds

entities.name: LSD
entities.role: psychedelic drug through which level 3 CEV patterns are relatively easily accessible

entities.name: Visual snow syndrome
entities.role: condition in which individuals see similar noise but have difficulty blocking it from conscious perception

entities.name: Blue-sky sprites
entities.role: entoptic phenomenon of dots darting around when staring at a bright blue sky, caused by white blood cells in retinal blood vessels; not related to CEV

entities.name: Hypnagogic hallucination
entities.role: process by which complex motion of patterns becomes directly visible when closing the eyes right before sleep or waking

entities.name: Isolation tank
entities.role: setting of complete sensory deprivation from which level 5 CEV can be entered

entities.name: REM sleep
entities.role: sleep stage during which the inhibitory system is inhibited, letting imagination run into perceptual systems
